nora: Heads-up from a customer onboarding call: Rust sample-app sporadically returns wrong embedding->query pairing after large async batches. Looks like a retry/merge edge.

kevin: Can you share the raw request/response? which endpoint/version?

nora: /v1/embeddings/rerank, batch size 2048 (chunked). Outgoing (redacted): 
```json
{"items":[{"id":"u10","text":"pricing"},{"id":"u11","text":"enable dedicated"},{"id":"u12","text":"api rate limits"}]}
```
Service-side merged response we captured (after auth refresh):
```json
{"results":[{"id":"u11","vector":[0.01,0.02,...],"dim":1536},{"id":"u10","vector":[...],"dim":1536},{"id":"u12","vector":[...],"dim":1536}]}
```
Rust helper then mapped by index and u10/u11 got swapped.

li: Repro'd by forcing an auth refresh mid-batch. Two contributing causes: 1) runtime shard merge appends partial replies (no stable sort), 2) current Rust helper uses positional mapping instead of id-keying. Also found a separate case where the quantized path emits base64 fp16 in field "embedding" and "dim" as string which makes numeric coercion fail in strict Rust types.

kevin: Oof. So order assumptions + schema drift + strict typing. Short-term client-side mitigation: always assemble results by id. Pseudo: let by_id: HashMap = resp.results.iter().map(|r| (r.id.clone(), r)).collect(); return req_items.iter().map(|i| by_id.get(&i.id)).collect(); Also accept both vector (numeric array) and embedding (b64), decode+convert fp16->f32, and validate dim as usize.

rust-sdk-bot: note: created draft PR #140 for the Rust helper normalization + fp16 decode. Includes fuzz test that shuffles server ordering and a fixture for base64 embedding.

li: Platform-side fix: please include original item.id in every response entry and prefer a canonical field name "vector" (float array). If quantized path must send b64, include both "vector_b64" and numeric "dim" as number. Also consider header X-Embedding-Format: "float32" | "fp16-b64" to make detection deterministic. Filing ticket PLATFORM-1428 was mentioned earlier; link it.

nora: For onboarding docs: adding short checklist for sample-apps: 1) assert vector length equals expected dim, 2) coerce numeric types and decode b64 fp16, 3) assemble response by id, fail loudly on missing ids, 4) prefer small chunk sizes during onboarding to reduce cross-shard merges.

kevin: Also note SDK parity drift: Python/Node still show differing field names in snippets (results vs items). We'll standardize docs and add a conformance test that loads both numeric and quantized fixtures and ensures all SDKs normalize to identical in-memory structs.

ci-bot: ci/test  #498: sampleapp-fuzz ran; shuffle-preserve test flaky on main, requeued.

li: Thanks. Nora, can you attach the repro trace to the PR and I'll ping platform with the X-Embedding-Format suggestion?

nora: Yep attached. Will update onboarding README and add a highlighted note: "Do not rely on response ordering; normalize by id."

kevin: Great. Once Rust PR lands we'll mark the flaky test as resolved and follow with docs parity cleanup.

nora: Thanks all, this should cut down a bunch of customer confusion during onboarding.
